articleTitle: Enhancement of pure-pursuit path-tracking algorithm with multi-goal selection
publicationTitle: 2019 1st IEEE International Conference on Gridding and Polytope Based Modeling and Control (GPMC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an enhancement to the popular pure-pursuit algorithm, widely used in robotics and automotive applications. The original algorithm is simple and straightforward as it depends only on the very basic attributes of the kinematic model of the target mechanical system. The algorithm is usually tuned by choosing a look-ahead distance of points from the reference trajectory. On the other hand, pure-pursuit suffers from considerable tuning weaknesses highly attributed to improper selection of look-ahead distance, resulting in poor tracking performance. Our method proposes the dynamic change of lookahead distance based on selecting multiple-goal points, thus aiming a curvature fitting more the reference trajectory. Our work was motivated by an ongoing robotics and autonomous vehicle research project at our university.

articleTitle: Grid-based LPV Modeling of Aeroelastic Aircraft with Parametrized Control Surface Design
publicationTitle: 2019 1st IEEE International Conference on Gridding and Polytope Based Modeling and Control (GPMC)
abstract: The fuel efficiency of future aircraft can be improved by reducing the weight and structure and by increasing the wingspan. This makes the aircraft structure more flexible and results in increased aeroservoelastic (ASE) effects. The use of active control systems to suppress ASE effects is an important aspect for future flight control systems. Control surface sizing is traditionally done in an iterative process. In such approach the size is determined based on engineering rules for which then the control laws are engineered. This approach, in addition to being time consuming, might not be applicable for future aircraft in which the flexible dynamics and rigid body control surface sizing can become coupled. Instead, a parametric control surface design approach can be applied, which to engineering rules takes limitations of control laws into consideration. Therefore, the control surfaces can be optimized in a single step with the control design. The aim of this paper is to develop a control oriented, control surface parametrized ASE model of the mini MUTT flexible aircraft, designed at the University of Minnesota. The ASE model is based on the integration of aerodynamics, structural dynamics and flight dynamics. A grid based linear parameter-varying (LPV) model is obtained from the nonlinear ASE model, which can serve as a basis for simultaneous control surface sizing and baseline/flutter suppression control synthesis optimization. The resulting parametric control surface LPV models are assessed with the help of numerical simulations including a gain scheduled baseline controller.

articleTitle: Tensor Product Transformation based Modelling of Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 1st IEEE International Conference on Gridding and Polytope Based Modeling and Control (GPMC)
abstract: State-space modelling theory is still a current topic of electrical machines in drive control. Induction machines can be described by nonlinear model leading to linear parameter varying (LPV) state-space model. In order to solve the above-mentioned highly nonlinear problem, Tensor Product (TP) transformation has been chosen. Big advantage of TP modelling are the short simulation time in MATLAB and speed controller can be designed easily.

articleTitle: Milestones in Developping the TP Model Transformation
publicationTitle: 2019 1st IEEE International Conference on Gridding and Polytope Based Modeling and Control (GPMC)
abstract: The goal of the paper is to introduce the key variants of the TP model transformation and to provide a practical and theoretical overview of this framework.

articleTitle: TP-based Control of the Crane Model
publicationTitle: 2019 1st IEEE International Conference on Gridding and Polytope Based Modeling and Control (GPMC)
abstract: Tensor product based model representation is a numerical technique to approximate the behavior of nonlinear systems. Based on the tensor product transformation a linear matrix inequality based controller design scheme can be applied efficiently. This framework is presented in the paper through the model of gantry crane.

articleTitle: A Grid-Based Model for Parameter Initialization in Non-Convex Optimization Tasks
publicationTitle: 2019 1st IEEE International Conference on Gridding and Polytope Based Modeling and Control (GPMC)
abstract: The role of nature versus nurture, and the relative strengths and weaknesses of evolutionary and gradient-based approaches have been the subject of fiery debate in the AI community for quite some time. As outlined in the paper, these approaches have unique advantages and at the same time by no means exhaust the list of tools necessary for designing artificially intelligent behavior. In particular, the importance of parameter initialization is often underestimated, as demonstrated by the widely publicized `lottery ticket hypothesis'. Following a discussion on why parameter initialization seems to be more important than previously acknowledged, a grid-based model is introduced which combines certain characteristics of evolutionary and gradient-based approaches with the goal of supporting robust parameter initialization.

articleTitle: Automated non-linear motion detection and estimation for MPI SPECT
publicationTitle: 2019 1st IEEE International Conference on Gridding and Polytope Based Modeling and Control (GPMC)
abstract: Uncontrolled motion in myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) may significantly influence the diagnostic value of a Single-Photon Computed Tomography (SPECT) study. The main goal is to develop advanced algorithms resulting in the most realistic and motion free datasets with high efficiency as opposed to data-driven solutions. Due to the motion phenomena the characterization - quantitative measurements - total perfusion deficit (TPD) or ejection fraction (EF) of the left ventricle (LV) will suffer significant distortion. An automatic method has been developed in attempt to solve the correction as a result of multiple artifacts obfuscated by unexpected patient motions. Nevertheless the SPECT heart images will suffer from additional artifacts, attenuation from intestines, uncontrolled imaging environments and parallel collimation. Moreover during the acquisition, different non-linear motion effects interfere the final measurements. A fully automatic method is invented, working in the complete detector field-of-view (FOV) in attempt to eliminate the linear and non-linear motions. The algorithm (non-linear mcARM) is based on the projection-reprojection scenario, with noise reduction by automatic heart mask estimation and optical flow to achieve the desired results. The performance is evaluated on mathematical phantom and patient database showing an increased accuracy in motion detection compared to the state of the art MoCo (Cedars-Sinai). The proposed method showed significant improvement over MoCo based on our findings on both phantom and patient studies calculating the TPD scores and by visual interpretation. Additionally to the improvement the method was able to detect non-linear movements in the datasets as well. Conclusion: A fully automatic complete FOV motion correction algorithm with non-linear motion detectability is introduced, with fast running times (2-4 seconds). Evaluation on patient and phantom studies showed promising results for the future.
